A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RetroDiT retrosynthesis study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrosynthesis experiments on USPTO-50k and USPTO-Full, including accuracy results, ablations, reaction-center sensitivity, and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports five-run uncertainty summaries for two USPTO-50k result rows.

M1.justification: Reaction-center-rooted ordering, RetroDiT with rotary embeddings, discrete flow matching, and the modular reaction-center predictor remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the architectural and implementation appendices retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use USPTO-50k and USPTO-Full for the same retrosynthesis tasks. Reaction-class breakdowns, round-trip evaluation, and simulated reaction-center corruption scenarios are retained without added coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Retroformer (Wan et al., 2022) to the USPTO-50k comparison in Table 1, reporting 53.2% Top-1 accuracy. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged; Ualign is retained with revised scores.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training settings, sampling budgets, and reaction-center corruption procedures are unchanged. The newly disclosed repeated-run information concerns uncertainty reporting rather than a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: The existing analysis of sensitivity to reaction-center accuracy in Appendix F.4 receives revised oracle and predicted-RC reference results in Table 8. Its tested corruption levels remain unchanged, as do the ordering, positional-embedding, backbone, reaction-class, and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports uncertainty for the oracle and predicted-RC rows and states that error bars use five independent runs with different random seeds. v1 supplied point estimates without this disclosure. Neither an increase over a previously stated run count nor the precise meaning of the ± values is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Retroformer and revises Ualign's Top-1/3/5/10 scores from 52.9/68.2/72.5/76.4 to 53.6/77.6/84.6/90.3. Table 8 replaces oracle and predicted-RC Top-1 values of 71.11 and 61.2 with 70.30 ± 0.43 and 60.29 ± 0.52, respectively, and revises their other Top-k entries. Table 9's additional decimal places are equivalent rounding, not changed performance.

T1.justification: The reaction-center definitions, flow-matching equations, conditional-independence assumptions, loss derivations in Appendix C, and predictor equations in Appendix E.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about positional inductive bias, efficiency, benchmark performance, and reaction-center prediction as the bottleneck. Their headline accuracy values are also retained.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly states that oracle reaction centers serve solely as an internal diagnostic upper bound, are not a deployment scenario, and should not replace predicted-RC results in direct end-to-end comparisons. Other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The extraction and ordering code listings, hyperparameters, hardware counts, training costs, and inference instructions are retained. Apart from the statistical disclosure assessed under E5, no substantive implementation or reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Retroformer reference and comparison and removes the Langley paper-writing reference. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to template-based, semi-template, and template-free approaches otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the oracle-use clarification and acknowledgments, replaces the preprint notice with proceedings information, and makes limited bibliographic edits. The section structure and nearly all explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a Retroformer row, and Table 8 widens to accommodate uncertainty values and an expanded caption. Existing figures, tables, and algorithms shift with text reflow, including Figure 1 and Table 3; the figures themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional comparator, explicit oracle-use qualification, and five-run uncertainty reporting are useful refinements. However, Table 8's revised 60.29 and 70.30 Top-1 summaries are not reconciled with the retained 61.2 and 71.1 headline results or Appendix F.4's old gain calculations. This matters to the claimed comparative advantage, including the comparison with EditRetro's 60.8 in Table 1. The benefits coexist with unresolved central performance reporting, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
